source_title: ED handoffs: observed practices and communication errors
locator: PubMed abstract, Methods and Results; lines 241-246 of rendered PubMed record
source_setting: Emergency physician patient handoffs at one major metropolitan teaching hospital ED; the abstract does not identify the study hospital
source_period: Eight weeks of observation; calendar dates not reported in abstract
unit: percent of handoffs with examination omissions (447/992 patient handoffs)
source_evidence_basis: Two investigators observed handoffs. Authors defined an error/omission by comparing clinically significant examination or laboratory findings in physician documentation with what was reported differently or omitted in verbal handoff. Examination omissions: 447 (45.1%); examination errors: 130 (13.1%). Fewer examination omissions were associated with use of written/electronic support.
limitations: Single center, observational, older study; denominator here is patient handoffs, not 110 sessions. Findings are against documentation and do not establish patient harm, causation, or rates at other hospitals. Abstract does not state observation dates.
inferred_scenario_use: Optional synthetic handoff variation: a documented examination finding is absent from verbal sign-out; learner may notice and clarify it. Do not use the study percentage as a scenario probability or local benchmark.

source_title: Interprofessional communication supporting clinical handover in emergency departments: An observation study
source_setting: Two acute hospital emergency departments in Victoria, Australia
source_period: Published 2017; observation calendar dates not reported in abstract
source_n: 66 observed change-of-shift handovers; focus groups with 34 nurse participants
source_evidence_basis: Observations and focus groups; qualitative content and thematic analysis. Four structural components emerged: antecedents; behaviours and interactions; content; delegation of ongoing care. Infrequent/ad hoc interprofessional communication and discipline-specific content/processes emerged as risks; themes included standard processes, teamwork/interactions, and communication practices.
limitations: Qualitative findings from two Australian EDs and nurse focus groups; no frequency estimate or causal effect. Transfer to a US ED or any specific hospital requires local validation.
inferred_scenario_use: Optional synthetic variation can test whether a learner establishes handoff context, shares relevant content across roles, and clarifies ownership of ongoing tasks. This is a design inference, not a required universal handoff format.

source_title: Workflow interruptions and stress at work: a mixed-methods study among physicians and nurses of a multidisciplinary emergency department
locator: Methods (Design/Setting/Sample and procedure; operational definition); Results, Figures 1-2; Discussion
source_setting: Emergency department of a major metropolitan academic community hospital in Augsburg, Germany
source_period: Published December 2017; observations on 20 randomly selected days; exact dates not stated
source_n: 77 matched observation/self-rating sessions; 116 hours 51 minutes observed; 877 interruptions; 791 interruptions with classified content
unit: interruptions per observed hour (877/116 h 51 min; paper reports 7.51/hour)
source_evidence_basis: Trained observers shadowed ED nurses and physicians during 90-minute sessions. Interruption defined as an unexpected task or communication causing discontinuation of the focal task and observable task switch. Common contents among 791 categorized events: parallel cases 240, current case 151, coordination 144. Parallel-case interruption events were associated with higher self-reported work stress; most interruption types showed no association.
limitations: One German academic ED, selected 90-minute observations, mixed-methods observational design; 80 sessions were scheduled but 77 matched. Rate depends on the paper's operational definition and denominator and must not be generalized as ED prevalence or a US/RWJUH estimate. Association does not establish causation or harm.
inferred_scenario_use: Optional synthetic interruption about a parallel patient or coordination can test task resumption and rechecking. Keep event timing and frequency authored as synthetic, not calibrated to the observed rate.

source_title: Patterns of Communication through Interpreters: A Detailed Sociolinguistic Analysis
locator: Abstract; Methods; Results; Questions Asked by Patients (especially reported counts at lines 270-275 in rendered full text)
source_setting: Primary-care physicians with high-volume Hispanic practices in New York, California, Texas, and Florida; dyslipidemia visits
source_period: First published May 31, 2006; collection dates not stated in article text inspected
source_n: 16 patients with 9 physicians; 13 interpreted Spanish-English encounters and 3 Spanish encounters with one bilingual physician
unit: reported count of patient questions answered directly by interpreter and not conveyed to physician; the paper also reports 28 direct questions across 13 interpreted visits
source_evidence_basis: Audio/video-recorded visits were transcribed and analyzed using sociolinguistic/discourse methods. In the Questions Asked by Patients section, authors report 28 direct patient questions across 13 interpreted visits and 8 answered directly by interpreter without translation to physician. The same passage reports a mean of 1.75 questions per visit, which is internally inconsistent with 28/13 (approximately 2.15). These counts are retained with the discrepancy flagged; no mean is used. Authors also report reduced/revised speech and little rapport-building small talk in interpreted visits.
limitations: Small, selected primary-care sample involving Spanish-speaking patients discussing dyslipidemia; interpreters in all interpreted examples were family members (n=2) or nursing/office staff (n=11), not a representative sample of professional interpreters. The reported question count and mean are internally inconsistent. Cannot infer ED rates, language-general behavior, current practice, or local interpreter conduct.
inferred_scenario_use: Optional synthetic variation: patient asks a question through an interpreter; learner directs communication to the patient and ensures the question and response are conveyed through the interpreter. Do not depict the pattern as characteristic of any real interpreter or hospital.
